new.name: October Caddis Soft Hackle
new.description: A burnt-orange dubbed body with a mottled partridge or hen collar, for the big autumn October caddis.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it through riffles on autumn afternoons when the big orange caddis are hatching.
steps: Tie in the wire and dub a fat orange body.
Rib it in even turns.
Dub a small dark thorax.
Wind two turns of partridge and whip finish.

new.name: Game Changer
new.description: An articulated baitfish built from several short shanks wrapped with chenille or brushes and trimmed to a tapered fish profile, so it swims with a lifelike S-curve.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it with pauses; the jointed body kicks side to side on every pull.
mats: Three or four articulated shanks with joint wire
Game Changer chenille or a synthetic brush
steps: Tie a short tail on the rear shank and wrap chenille forward, stroking the fibres back.
Join each shank with a short loop of wire and repeat, making each section slightly bigger.
Finish on the hook with the fullest section.
Trim to a baitfish taper, colour the back with a marker and glue on the eyes.

new.name: Holy Grail Caddis
new.description: A beaded hare's mask emerger with a pearl flash rib, a pheasant tail wing case and partridge legs.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it before and during caddis hatches, or swing it at the end of the drift.
steps: Add the bead, start the thread and tie in the flash.
Dub a rough body and rib it.
Tie in pheasant tail for the wing case and dub the thorax.
Tie in partridge fibres each side as legs, pull the wing case over and whip finish behind the bead.

new.name: Green Drake
new.description: A big olive dun with a moose hair tail, olive dubbed body and grizzly-dyed-olive hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in early summer when the big drakes come off, often in the afternoon or on overcast days.
steps: Tie in a moose hair tail.
Dub a tapered olive body.
Wind the hackle through the front third and whip finish.

new.name: Veverka's Mantis Shrimp
new.description: A realistic mantis shrimp for the flats, with a long segmented body, bead-chain eyes and a soft, buggy profile.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it in short, sharp pulls near tailing bonefish and permit, or for redfish over mud.
mats: Bead chain or burnt mono eyes
Fine bucktail and a few strands of flash
Tan or olive dubbing, palmered with grizzly
Thin foam or Thin Skin, segmented with thread
steps: Tie in the eyes and antennae at the bend.
Tie in the shell and a hackle.
Dub the body forward and palmer the hackle through it.
Pull the shell over, segment it with thread and whip finish.

new.name: Red Tag
new.description: A peacock herl body with a bright red tag and a brown hackle collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it wet in rivers and lakes, or tied dry for grayling.
steps: Tie in a short red yarn tag.
Tie in the wire and herl, wind a full herl body and rib it.
Wind two turns of brown hen and whip finish.

new.name: Foam Beetle
new.description: A black foam back folded over a peacock herl body, with rubber legs and a bright sighter.
new.fishing_tips: Splat it under overhanging trees on summer days.
steps: Tie in a foam strip at the bend.
Wind a peacock herl body.
Pull the foam over and tie it down, leaving a short head.
Add legs each side and a sighter on top.

new.name: Royal Coachman
new.description: The famous attractor: golden pheasant tippet tail, peacock body split by a red floss band, white duck wings and brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: An attractor for fast mountain streams.
mats: Peacock herl with a red floss band
steps: Tie in the wings upright and divided.
Tie in the tail.
Wind herl, red floss, then herl again.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Madam X
new.description: A deer hair body and wing with a bullet head and white rubber legs: a buggy hopper, stonefly or caddis suggestion.
new.fishing_tips: Twitch it so the legs move; great in pocket water.
steps: Tie in a bundle of hair at the bend for the tail.
Wrap thread forward over it.
Tie in hair facing forward, then fold it back as a bullet head and wing.
Tie in the legs at the collar and whip finish.

new.name: Black Beauty Midge
new.description: A black thread midge larva ribbed with fine copper and a small black dubbed head.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it small in tailwaters, under an indicator or as a dropper.
steps: Wrap a slim black thread abdomen.
Rib it with copper wire.
Dub a tiny thorax and whip finish.

new.name: Mayer's Mini Leech
new.description: A small, simple leech: a marabou tail and a body of the same marabou wrapped on, with a few strands of flash.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it under an indicator in tailwaters, or strip it slowly in lakes.
steps: Tie in a marabou tail.
Twist the remaining marabou into a rope and wrap it forward.
Add a couple of flash strands and whip finish.

new.name: Sucker Spawn
new.description: A cluster of loose yarn loops that looks like a clump of sucker or trout eggs.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it in spring when suckers are spawning.
steps: Tie in a strand of yarn.
Wrap it in small loops along the shank.
Tie off and whip finish.

new.name: Bully's Bluegill Spider
new.description: A weighted chenille body with white rubber legs. Simple and deadly on panfish.
new.fishing_tips: Let it sink slowly near cover; strikes come on the drop.
steps: Add a few wraps of wire.
Tie in the chenille and wrap a fat body.
Tie rubber legs in at the middle and front, whip finish.

new.name: Drunk & Disorderly
new.description: An articulated streamer with a foam diving head that makes it dart erratically on the strip.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it on a sinking line: it dives and swings side to side, then floats up on the pause.
steps: Tie a marabou tail and body on the rear hook.
Join it to the front shank and tie in the collar.
Glue on the foam head, cut at an angle to dive.
Add the eyes.

new.name: Near Nuff Sculpin
new.description: A sculpin with a rabbit strip back, palmered body and wide flared pectoral fins, weighted to bounce on the bottom.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep and slow along the bottom.
steps: Weight the hook and tie in the rabbit strip tail.
Dub the body and palmer the hackle.
Tie in fins each side.
Dub a wide flat head and whip finish.

new.name: Balanced Leech
new.description: A jig-hook leech balanced on a pin with a bead so it hangs level under an indicator, with a marabou tail and a seal fur body.
new.fishing_tips: Hang it under an indicator in lakes; wind ripple gives it life.
steps: Glue a short pin along the shank with the bead on its end.
Tie in a marabou tail with a little flash.
Dub a rough body and pick it out.
Whip finish.

new.name: Smoke Jumper
new.description: A slim midge emerger with a thread body, wire rib, peacock thorax and a CDC puff wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the film or just under during midge hatches.
steps: Wrap a slim ribbed thread body.
Tie in the CDC so it forms a small puff.
Wrap a peacock thorax and whip finish.

new.name: Grizzly King
new.description: A green-bodied wet fly with a red tail, gold rib, grizzly hackle and a mallard flank wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it wet in lakes and streams, especially for brook trout.
steps: Tie in a red tail and the rib.
Wrap a green body and rib it.
Tie a grizzly beard or collar.
Tie a mallard wing on top and whip finish.

new.name: Spanish Bullet
new.description: A slim, heavy perdigon-style nymph with a coated thread body and hot-spot collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on a Euro rig in fast water.
mats: Thread, with a pearl or tinsel rib
steps: Add the bead and tie in a sparse tail.
Wrap a slim tapered thread body and rib it.
Add a hot-spot collar.
Coat the whole body with UV resin and cure it.

new.name: Mohair Leech
new.description: A simple leech of brushed-out mohair yarn with a bead head and a marabou tail.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it slowly or hang it under an indicator in lakes.
steps: Add the bead and a marabou tail with flash.
Wrap the mohair forward.
Brush it out so the fibres flow back, then whip finish.

new.name: Gummy Minnow
new.description: A translucent baitfish of pearl flash wrapped in a soft clear body, glued into a minnow shape.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast for false albacore, stripers and snook chasing small bait.
mats: Pearl flash inside a clear soft body
steps: Tie a pearl flash core along the shank.
Fold the clear body material around it and trim to a minnow shape.
Colour the back, add eyes and coat it.

new.name: EP Spawning Shrimp
new.description: A slim shrimp of EP fibres with a bright egg sac, bead-chain eyes and a soft weed guard.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it in short hops for bonefish and redfish on the flats.
mats: EP fibres with a little flash
steps: Tie the eyes near the eye of the hook.
Dub a small orange egg sac at the bend.
Tie in sparse EP fibres and legs so the fly rides hook-up.
Whip finish.

new.name: Ray Charles
new.description: A sow bug of a pearl Flashabou shellback over grey ostrich herl.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it in weedy tailwaters.
steps: Tie in the flash at the bend.
Wind the ostrich herl forward.
Pull the flash over the back and whip finish.

new.name: Red Fox Squirrel Nymph
new.description: A buggy fox squirrel nymph: a squirrel hair tail, a lighter belly-fur abdomen ribbed with gold and a darker back-fur thorax with partridge legs.
new.fishing_tips: An all-round searching nymph that suggests many mayflies and stoneflies.
steps: Weight the shank and tie in the tail and rib.
Dub the abdomen and rib it.
Dub a rough thorax.
Wind a turn of partridge and whip finish.

new.name: CDC Bubble Caddis
new.description: A caddis emerger with a CDC wing that traps air bubbles like a hatching sedge.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the film when caddis are hatching but the fish won't take a full dry.
steps: Dub a slim body.
Tie in a CDC wing low over the back.
Dub a small thorax and whip finish.

new.name: Green Peter
new.description: A green seal fur body with a gold rib and palmered ginger hackle, a hen pheasant wing and a ginger collar. A lough pattern for the big Green Peter sedge.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on the top dropper on Irish and Scottish loughs in late summer, especially in the evening.
steps: Tie in the rib and body hackle.
Dub the body, palmer the hackle and rib it.
Tie in a rolled hen pheasant wing.
Wind a ginger collar and whip finish.

new.name: Jersey Herd
new.description: A classic stillwater lure: a copper tinsel body under a peacock herl back, an orange hackle collar and a peacock tail.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it in lakes for fry-feeding trout.
steps: Tie in the peacock herl with the tips left as a tail.
Build a floss underbody and cover it with copper tinsel.
Pull the herl over the back.
Wind an orange collar and whip finish.

new.name: Cruncher Nymph
new.description: A slim pheasant tail body with a pearl rib and a short hen hackle; a great buzzer and nymph suggestion.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slowly on a floating line in lakes.
steps: Tie in a short tail and the rib.
Wrap a pheasant tail body and rib it.
Dub a small thorax.
Wind a turn of hen and whip finish.

new.name: Skykomish Sunrise
new.description: A Pacific Northwest steelhead classic: red chenille body ribbed with silver, red and yellow hackle and a white wing.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for summer steelhead.
mats: White calf tail or polar bear substitute
steps: Tie in a red and yellow tail and the rib.
Wrap a chenille body and rib it.
Wind red and yellow hackle.
Tie in a white wing and whip finish.

new.name: Lady Caroline
new.description: A Spey fly with an olive and brown wool body, long grey heron-style hackle, golden pheasant tail and a bronze mallard wing.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it slowly for Atlantic salmon and steelhead in cold water.
steps: Tie in the tail, ribs and hackle.
Wrap the body and wind the long hackle between the ribs.
Add a throat.
Tie in bronze mallard wings, tented low, and whip finish.

new.name: Wickham's Fancy
new.description: A gold-bodied fancy fly with palmered ginger hackle, starling wings and a ginger tail. Fished wet or dry.
new.fishing_tips: Try it during sedge and olive hatches, or as a general attractor on chalkstreams.
steps: Tie in the tail, wire and hackle.
Wrap a gold body, palmer the hackle and rib it.
Tie in the wing slips and whip finish.

new.name: Dunkeld
new.description: A gold-bodied wet fly with an orange palmer, a golden pheasant crest tail, bronze mallard wing and jungle cock cheeks.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on loch drifts and for sea trout.
steps: Tie in the crest tail.
Wrap a gold body, palmer the orange hackle and rib it.
Tie in the mallard wing and cheeks, whip finish.

new.name: Quigley Cripple
new.description: A crippled mayfly hanging in the film: a marabou shuck and dubbed abdomen sinking below, a deer hair wing and hackle on top.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it to selective risers during mayfly hatches.
mats: Marabou or dubbing, ribbed with wire
steps: Tie in a marabou tail and twist it into a short abdomen.
Dub the thorax.
Tie in a deer hair wing angled forward over the eye.
Wind a few turns of hackle behind the wing and whip finish.

new.name: Eggstasy Egg
new.description: A soft, translucent egg of Eggstasy yarn wound into a ball.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it near spawning fish.
steps: Tie in a strand of yarn.
Wrap it into a round ball, stroking the fibres back.
Whip finish.

new.name: Bird's Nest
new.description: A shaggy nymph with a mallard flank tail and legs, a rough dubbed body and a copper rib.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it or swing it; it suggests caddis pupae and mayfly nymphs.
mats: Rough hare's ear or Australian opossum
Mallard flank, wound as a collar
steps: Tie in a short tail and the rib.
Dub a rough body and rib it.
Wind a mallard flank collar, dub over the base and whip finish.

new.name: Sprout Midge
new.description: A midge emerger with a slim thread body, a peacock thorax and an upright foam or poly sprout of wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it to fish sipping midges in the film.
steps: Wrap a slim ribbed thread body.
Tie in a short upright wing.
Wrap a peacock thorax and whip finish.

new.name: Missing Link
new.description: A low-riding caddis/mayfly emerger: a thread body, a hair wing and a parachute hackle wound around a short post.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it when fish are taking emergers they won't refuse.
steps: Wrap a slim body.
Tie in a deer hair wing and a short post.
Wind a parachute hackle around the post and whip finish.

new.name: Spent Partridge Caddis
new.description: A spent egg-laying caddis: a peacock thorax and a partridge wing tied flat over the back with a few turns of hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it flush in the film during evening egg-laying flights.
mats: Brown and grizzly, a few turns
steps: Dub a slim body.
Tie a partridge feather flat over the back.
Wrap a peacock thorax and a little hackle, then trim it flat underneath.
Whip finish.

new.name: Parachute Ant
new.description: Two dubbed humps with a parachute hackle and a bright post at the waist: easy to see and floats well.
new.fishing_tips: Drop it along banks on summer days.
mats: Black or cinnamon dubbing, two humps
steps: Dub a round rear hump.
Tie in a post at the waist and wind a parachute hackle.
Dub a smaller front hump and whip finish.
